changes.summary: A federal judge dismissed DOJ's Utah voter-file suit with prejudice after rejecting the Title III theory as applied to the statewide list.
changes.duplicate_review: The ruling resolves the Utah lawsuit already described in NAT-2026-09-10-008. The same parties, voter-file demand, statutory theory and litigation lifecycle require a same-event update rather than a new canonical count.

source_inspections.origin_group: U.S. District Court for the District of Utah
source_inspections.evidence_extract: In United States v. Henderson, Case No. 2:26-cv-00166-DBB, Document 68, filed and signed October 23, 2026, Judge David Barlow held that Utah's statewide voter registration list falls outside Title III because the lieutenant governor develops it rather than receiving it as a record that comes into her possession. The court denied the attorney general's motion to compel, granted the defendants' motions to dismiss, dismissed the complaint with prejudice, and did not reach alternative arguments concerning the demand's basis and purpose, state-law redactions, or the Privacy Act.
source_inspections.hash_scope: SHA-256 of the exact normalized evidence extract retained here, not a claim of hashing the complete PDF.

source_inspections.evidence_extract: KSL reported on October 23, 2026 that Judge David Barlow dismissed DOJ's suit seeking Utah's voter rolls, quoted the court's statutory holding, recorded Henderson's response, and reported that DOJ did not immediately comment. KSL also reported that the case was dismissed with prejudice and that DOJ had lost more than 25 similar cases.
